reasoning: A QG3 quasigroup satisfies Stein's third law: (i*j)*(j*i) = i, combined with idempotence i*i = i. It is a known result in combinatorics that idempotent QG3 quasigroups (Stein quasigroups) of order n exist only when n ≡ 0 or 1 (mod 4). Since 7 ≡ 3 (mod 4), no such quasigroup of order 7 exists. This was confirmed by both a Z3 SMT solver returning UNSAT and a backtracking search finding no solution. The non-existence follows from a parity/counting argument on the structure imposed by the QG3 identity on idempotent Latin squares.
